metadata.title: Why a sepsis alarm in hundreds of hospitals learned to wait for the doctor
metadata.topic: THE LIMITS OF AI · THE DATA-WORLD GAP
metadata.purpose: Answer one real question in the Plain register: why did an AI sepsis alarm in hundreds of hospitals wait for the doctor? Lands the carry-out that a model cannot warn you about an event if its strongest feature is the trace of you already reacting to it.
metadata.anchor_pair: B03 -> B08 (The clinical timeline to the suspicion loop)
metadata.one_flag: B10 — data contains the order feature, but not the clinical intent

beats.narration_text: When an AI early-warning system clears hospital validation with high accuracy, we assume it predicts sepsis before doctors notice. In reality, it learned to wait for the doctor. Let's see why.

shot.new_visual_element: Writer types naive question, hesitates on 'predicts sepsis before doctors notice', corrects to 'fires after doctors already suspect'

props.text:
If an AI hospital alarm
has high validation accuracy,
can we assume it predicts
sepsis before doctors notice?

beats.note: B00 is Remotion (BrutalistHesitantWriter) per course-skepticism SKILL.md. Writer types naive framing, hesitates, corrects to misconception. Liam reads over typing animation.

beats.narration_text: A proprietary sepsis early-warning model was deployed across hundreds of hospitals. Sepsis is deadly and hours matter, so a machine learning model forecasting deterioration promised to save lives.

shot.new_visual_element: Hospital network deployment, proprietary model badge, hours-to-treatment stakes

production_viz.label: Deployment across hundreds of hospitals
production_viz.mechanic: Hospital network nodes and early-warning alert badge showing hours-to-treatment stakes

beats.narration_text: The model cleared internal testing with flying colors. But when independent researchers evaluated it across thousands of hospitalizations — Wong et al. in 2021 — it missed most sepsis cases and flooded wards with alerts.

shot.new_visual_element: Internal clearance versus Wong et al. 2021 external evaluation disconnect

production_viz.label: Internal clearance vs external evaluation
production_viz.mechanic: Split card comparing internal validation clearance with independent 2021 external evaluation

beats.narration_text: To see why the metrics collapsed, look at the sequence of care. A patient is admitted. Over hours and days, doctors and nurses observe vital signs, notice subtle deterioration, and decide when to act.

shot.new_visual_element: Linear clinical care timeline planted: admission, bedside observations, clinical decision

production_viz.label: The clinical care timeline
production_viz.mechanic: Horizontal timeline anchor: patient admission, serial observations, bedside judgment

beats.narration_text: The naive mental model assumes the AI acts as an independent forecaster, spotting hidden physiological signals in raw vitals hours before bedside clinicians notice anything wrong.

shot.new_visual_element: Naive model of AI independently forecasting ahead of human clinicians

production_viz.label: The independent forecaster assumption
production_viz.mechanic: Diagram of AI supposedly leaping ahead of clinical awareness using raw vitals

beats.narration_text: That assumption breaks when you examine what features the model was actually using. Alongside temperature and pulse, the algorithm drank in clinical workflow orders.

shot.new_visual_element: Feature vector breakdown: physiological signals versus workflow order entries

production_viz.label: Feature vector breakdown
production_viz.mechanic: Two columns of features: physical vitals versus clinical action orders

beats.narration_text: Here is how hospital medicine works. When an experienced physician suspects sepsis, their immediate next step is to order diagnostic lab work — specifically, a blood culture.

shot.new_visual_element: Physician clinical suspicion leading directly to diagnostic blood culture order

production_viz.label: Clinician suspicion and blood culture order
production_viz.mechanic: Bedside clinician forming suspicion and entering diagnostic blood-culture order

beats.narration_text: That order enters the digital record. The model's algorithm traces that sudden new event, recognizes a strong statistical correlation with sepsis, and its internal risk score spikes.

shot.new_visual_element: Manim move trace: order enters data stream, feature vector updates, risk score spikes

production_viz.label: Tracing the order into the feature vector
production_viz.mechanic: Manim move TRACE: blood culture order enters data log; model traces the event and risk score spikes

beats.narration_text: The result is the suspicion loop. The doctor suspects sepsis, so the doctor orders blood cultures. The model sees the order, fires an urgent sepsis alert, and sends it straight back to the doctor who already suspected it.

shot.new_visual_element: The circular suspicion loop: suspicion -> order -> feature -> alert -> doctor

production_viz.label: The suspicion loop payoff
production_viz.mechanic: Full cycle diagram: Clinician suspicion -> Blood-culture order -> Model feature -> Model alert -> Clinician who already acted

beats.narration_text: To an automated scoring script, this looks like brilliant performance. The model alerted, and the patient indeed had sepsis. But the alert was downstream of the human judgment it claimed to anticipate.

shot.new_visual_element: Automated evaluation scoring script registering false success as True Positive

production_viz.label: Evaluation script registers false success
production_viz.mechanic: Validation scorecard marking True Positive because alert and sepsis co-occur, ignoring temporal order

beats.narration_text: One flag — no machine learning model can detect this flaw from inside its own training data. The data contains the culture order, but not the clinical intent that created it.

shot.new_visual_element: The data-world boundary: features inside the frame versus intent outside

production_viz.label: The data-world frame boundary
production_viz.mechanic: Boxed data frame showing observed features vs unobserved clinical intent outside the frame

beats.narration_text: In one direction, high predictive accuracy in the training log is not proof of an early warning. A model that echoes human decisions can look mathematically perfect while offering zero forecasting lead time.

shot.new_visual_element: Direction A: High Predictive Accuracy ≠ Forecasting Lead Time

production_viz.label: Direction A: High Accuracy ≠ Forecasting Lead Time
production_viz.mechanic: HIGH PREDICTIVE ACCURACY ≠ EARLY FORECASTING LEAD TIME, struck through with terracotta

beats.narration_text: In the other direction, the algorithm did not calculate incorrectly. It found the strongest statistical pattern in the data. The failure was mistaking a trace of clinician suspicion for an independent discovery.

shot.new_visual_element: Direction B: Correct Statistical Math ≠ Valid Epistemic Claim

production_viz.label: Direction B: Correct Math ≠ Valid Claim
production_viz.mechanic: Math performed flawlessly on available features; epistemic premise failed

beats.narration_text: An early-warning model cannot warn you about an event if its strongest feature is the trace of you already reacting to it.

props.quote: An early-warning model cannot warn you about an event if its strongest feature is the trace of you already reacting to it.

beats.narration_text: Your turn. Here's the prompt — read it with me. Audit a predictive model in your workflow. Which of its top input features are actually traces of human decisions responding to the outcome it claims to predict? Liam, in for Bear.
